RAJYA SABHA      [20 December, 2000] 
Issuance of photo identity cards in Jammu and Kashmir 
*441. SHRI S. RAMACHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Central Government have advised the State Government of 
Jammu and Kashmir to issue photo identity cards to all male habitants in the age 
group of 16 to 60 years living within 25 Kms. of the Line of 
Control/International Border; 
(b) if so, the State Government's reaction thereto; 
 
(c) by when the work of issuing such cards would be taken up; and 
(d) what are the reasons for not issuing such cards to the females living in the 
same area? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO): (a) to (d) A statement 
is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (c) The J&K Action Plan contains as part of measures suggested to 
check infiltration, a recommendation that the State Government issue identity 
cards to all male habitants in the age group of 16 to 60 years living within 25 
Kms. on the Line of Contra1 (LoC)/International Border (IB) in J&K. The State 
Government h? reported that the system of identity cards has already been put in 
place within 5 Kms. of the LoC and the modalities for extending the scheme are 
being worked out by the State Government, Central Government would reimburse 
the costs under Security Related Expenditure. 
(d) The recommendation for issuance of identity cards was made with a view 
to facilitating identification of infiltrators particularly foreign mercenaries and as 
the infiltrating terrorists are all males, the group that had prepared the J&K Action 
Plan, had felt that issuing of identity cards to males would prove sufficient for 
this purpose. 
SHRI S. RAMACHANDRAN PILLAI: Sir, I would like to know from the 
hon. Minister whether the Union Government and the State Government of Jammu 
and Kashmir have sat together and discussed about the details of the assessment 
about the persons who are living within that particular area, the cost involved, the 
timeframe for its completion and the progress so far made. 
SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO: Mr. Chairman, Sir. as 
far as this scheme is concerned, photo identity

cards are issued to the males living within 25 kilometres of the Line of 
Control and the International Border. The Jammu and Kashmir State 
Government got a survey conducted by the Kashmir Police for issuing the 
photo identity cards. They have estimated that there are 8,30,000 males living 
in that area. The State Government proposes to issue photo identity cards to 
the males in the age group of 16—60 years, in the 25 kilometres belt along 
the Line of Control and the International Border. The State Government 
wants the Ministry of Home Affairs to  allocate Rs. 1.4 crores towards the 
cost of issuing the photo identity cards. Under the Security Related 
Expenditure, the State Government is provided with Rs. 50 lakhs this year 
and Rs. 1 crore next year. It is made under the Security Related Expenditure. 
As far as the State is concerned, it will be completed within six months of 
starting the scheme, that is, 2002. We expect that this will be completed by 
2002

hon. Minister whether the issuance of the photo identity cards is based on a

would be the course of action open to the Government? 
SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO: Sir, it is not based on 
any statutory legislation. It is bacause  of the particular situation along the 
LoC and to check the infiltration into the country. This special programme 
has been taken up by the Government pursuant to the recommendations given

country. That is why this question has arisen. As far as the LoC and 
international borders are concerned, im mediate steps are necessary and it is 
all the more necessary to* take this st ep. Therefore, only in  these areas, this 
step has been taken. As and when the question arises, it will be dealt with.

RAJYA SABHA       [20 December, 2000] 
SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE: Sir, the hon. Minister has pointed out, 
that as per the assessment—if I have heard him correctly—the work would 
be completed by 2002. The question to which I would like to have an answer 
from the hon. Minister is this. In-between a situation may arise, as it has 
arisen in some areas. We have received certain complaints from certain areas 
that the persons who have not got proper photo identity cards are, sometimes, 
subjected to harassment because a small section of the population is getting 
the photo identity cards and another section is left out. 
The Police and the security forces ar e harassing them as they do not 
possess the identity card. They are subjected to examination, and, sometimes, 
they are harassed. Such complaints come  in. The Action Plan was formulated 
quite some time back, but up till now, you have completed only 5 kms. from 
the LoC. And, there, the number of people is comparatively less. When you 
go further interior, the density of the population would be more. So, more 
persons are to be covered. Keeping the present situation in view, it would not 
be that easy merely saying that you will be able to do it by 2002. The scheme 
is quite good, and it is one effective way to prevent infiltration. But I would 
like to know what safeguards the Government is going to take to ensure that 
until the time they are able to provide identity cards to all the people, there is 
no unnecessary harassment, because this is a sensitive issue; a lot of 
complaints have come. Let this not be another cause for harassment by the 
security forces or by the police authorities or by other administrative 
authorities. I would like to know whether the Government can contemplate 
some sort of safeguard during the interim period when identity cards would not 
be provided, especially, in areas where a section of the people has received 
the card and another section of the people has not received it. 
SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO: Sir, now, the State 
Government's is expediting the scheme pertaining to 8,30,000 people who are 
living within a radius of 20 kms. from the LoC and the International Border. 
Already, the State Government has issued photo identity cards to people 
within a 5 km. area, and th ey need an additional expenditure of Rs. 50 lakhs 
for updating the cards. Sir, so far, there has been no objection from the 
people within the 5 km. radius area but, in future, if anything comes to our 
notice, then it can be looked into.

Statement-I 
Functions of Proposed Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) 
BEE will primarily function as a fac ilitator in the promotion of energy 
conservation and efficiency Programme by coordinating with various 
concerned agencies such as BIS, Ce ntral and State Government agencies. 
Non-govemrncntal agencies, consumers and manufacturers and their 
associations, different laboratories and financial institutions and external 
multi-lateral and bi-lateral aiding agencies. 
The bureau may exercise such powers and performs such functions as 
may be assigned to it by or under the proposed Act and in particular include 
the following functions:—  
(i)      The BEE will recommend to the Central Government the norms for 
process and energy consumption standards for any equipment, 
appliance which consumes, generates, transmits or supplied energy. 
(ii)    The BEE will re commend to the Central Government the particulars 
required to be displayed on label on equipment or on appliances and 
manner of their display. 
(iii)  The BEE recommend to the Central Government for notifying any 
user or class or users of energy as designated consumer having 
regard to intensity or quantity of energy used by it. 
(iv)    The BEE will prescribe guidelines for energy conservation building 
code and coordinate with the States for their adaptation and 
notification. 
(v)    The BEE will take all measures necessary to create awareness and 
disseminate information regarding efficient use of energy and its 
conservation. 
(vi)   The BEE will take all measures necessary to train personnel and 
specialists in the techniques of efficient use of energy and its 
conservation.

testing facilities for certification and testing for energy consumption 
of equipment and appliances. 
(x)       The BEE will formulate and facilitate implementation of pilot projects

and its conservation. 
(xi)    The BEE will promote use of energy efficient process, equipment,

projects.

acquired by the State Governments th rough the imposition of ceilings on

addition, Government wastelands ana* Bhoodan lands are also distributed to 
the rural poor. Since the inception of the programme till March, 2000, an area of 
52.90 lakh acres of ceiling surplus land s, 147.47 lakh acres of Government 
Wastelands and 21.75 lakh acres of Bhoodan Lands have been distributed to the 
rural poor, including SCsSTs and OBCs. * Nearly 50% of the ceiling surplus

Policy on coal exploration 
3304. SHRI B. J. PANDA: Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to state: 
(a) the policy of Government with regard to the mining and exploration of

48 

RAJYA SABHA       [20 December, 2000] 
(b) whether private sector participation has been invited in the coal mines sector; 
and 
(c) if so, to what extent and what will be its impact on the nationalized 
coal mines? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF COAL (SHRI N. T. 
SHANMUGAM): (a) to (c) Private coal mines were nationalized in 1972 and 1973 
in - <*er to augment coal production in the country by adopting advance mining 
technology. In 1993, the Central Government allowed private participation by 
allowing coal mining by companies engaged in pronation of iron & steel, power 
generation and washing of coal obtained from a mine for captive use only. Later on 
companies engaged in cement production were also allowed coal mining for 
their captive use. 
Recent assessment about the demand and supply position of coal over the next 
decade made by the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Coal shows a gap 
of 41.94 million tonnes, 162.28 million tonnes and 260.30 million tonnes during

mobilize adequate resources to step up coal production to meet the ever 
increasing demand. Therefore, the Government has introduced a Bill in the 
Rajya Sabha to amend the Coal Mines (Nationalization) Act, 1973 for enabling 
non-captive coal and lignite minning as well as exploration of coal and lignite 
resources by the Indian Companies. This Bill does not seek to privatise any of 
the nationalised coal companies.

Excess Payment to Contractor by DG, Naval Project, Mumbai 
3319. DR. BIPLAB DASGUPTA: Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the incorrect decision by the Director General, 
Naval Project, Mumbai to allow the refund to the contractor for excess 
consumption of cement led to extra expenditure of about Rs. 64 crores; 
(b) if so, whether the amount has since been recovered from the contractor; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether it is also a fact that the Navy has used a life expired sonar 
cable causing loss of sonar dome; and 
(e) if so, what steps have been taken so as to.stop recurrence of such 
instance in future? 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERN ANDES): (a) to 
(e) The Director General Naval Project, Mumbai, had concluded a contract for 
pre-casting of 52,000 cubic meter of concrete cement blocks for a Naval project. 
The contract specified the technical sp ecification for the concrete mix for 
ensuring the required strength and workability characteristic. It also specified the 
minimum quantity (400 Kg) of cement to be used in each cubic meter of 
concrete mix. However additional cement beyond the specified minimum 
quantity, was used by the contractor to achieve the desired quality. The actual 
quantity of cement used was between 410 Kg and 460 Kg for each cubic 
meter of concrete mix as against the minimum quantity of 400 Kg specified in 
the contract. In the period January, 1996 to July, 1998, DGNP was effecting 
deductions from the contractor for the cost of additional quantity of the 
departmentally supplied cement from the payments due to contractor. The 
contractor had represented against such deductions on the ground that use of 
additional cement was an-essential technical requirement of the department, 
based on the laboratory test, for which he was not liable, as his original 
quotation for the work was based on the minimum quantity specified in the 
tender document. 
65 

RAJYA SABHA       [20 December, 2000] 
The contention of the contractor was examined by Director General Naval 
Projects, Mumbai and was considered to be valid. As such, DGNP agreed to 
refund Rs. 63.81 lakhs for deductions made. 
Audit have commented on the decision of Director General, Naval Project, 
Mumbai to refund the cost of excess consumption cement to the contractor. The 
observation of audit in the matter is being examined. 
The electronics end of the Towed Sonar was lost from an Indian Naval Ship in 
September, 1998 due to localized corrosion at the joints of the towing cables and 
not due to use of life expired cable. Necessary corrective actions have been 
implemented to prevent occurrence of  corrosion by improved protective 
material.

implement the recommendations of the Commission in toto, the matter still

can be resolved only with the willing co-operation of the State Governments

3380. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of POWER be

captioned "India's power reforms are a non-starter" published in the 'Business

(c) the steps takeivfcroposed to be taken regarding the problems7 raised in the

(d) what steps have been taken or proposed to be taken to make India an 
alternative destination for investment in power sector? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRIMATI 
JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) to (d) Financial closure of a number of 
Independent Power Projects (IPPs) is held up due to non-availability of 
escrowable capacity with the SEBs to provide payment security to these 
projects. The various steps taken by Government regarding the problems raised 
in the said news-item and to make India an attractive destination for investment in 
power sector include the following:— 
(i) The issue of reforms of SEBs wa s discussed in the Power Ministers 
Conference held in February, 2000. It was resolved that reforms must be 
undertaken with determination, vigour and a sense of urgency. The key 
elements of the reforms strategy are:—  
(a) Energy Audit at all levels.

December, 2001.

distribution system by taking sub-station as a unit on a 
priority basis. 
If   the   above   appears   unattainable   in   the  existing  set   up, 
corporatization/cooperatization/privatization   of   distribution,   would 
have to be undertaken.

agreed that financing of IPPs would be linked with achievement of

(SHRIMATI   JAYAWANTI   MEHTA):    (a)   and   (b)   Energy 
Management Centre (EMC) was established in the year 1989 under the

STATEMENT BY PRIME MINISTER 
Government* Peace Initiative in Jammu and Kashmir 
THE PRIME MINISTER (SHRI ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE): Sir, before 
the Winter Session of the Parliament concludes, and the House rises 
for the festival of Id and Christmas, I wish to take this opportunity and 
share with all hon. Members, the Government's assessment of the 
situation in Jammu and Kashmir, also along the LoC. 
Following my announcement of 19th November, that during 
the holy month of Ramzan, our security forces would not initiate 
operations against the militants, also expressing a hope that along 
the LoC too, infiltration would cease, there, have been some 
encouraging developments. Certain other aspects, however, remain 
as our continuing concerns. 
The Government is greatly heartened by the response of the 
citizens, political parties and other organisations in the State of 
Jammu and Kashmir. Our peace initiative has been widely welcomed 
there. A distinctly different and a more optimistic mood now prevails in 
that State. The constituency for peace has expanded significantly. 
There has also been a decline in incidents of terrorist 
violence in that State. Activities, however, of organisations like 
Lashkar-e-Tayaaba and Harkat-ul-Mujahedin continue, resulting in 
most unfortunate and regrettable loss of innocent civilian lives, also of 
the personnel of our security forces. The Government remains firm In 
its resolve to combating these and other challenges, also to defeating 
their inhuman and nefarious designs. 
There has been a recognisable decline, too, in attempts at 
cross-LOC and cross-IB infiltration of terrorists. This must cease 
entirely. The Government is committed to achieving this end.

As the initiator of the dialogue process with Pakistan, India

from Jammu and Kashmir to join as equal partners in India's march to 
prosperity.

SHRI KA. RA. SUBBIAN (Tamil Nadu): Thank you, Madam, 
for having given me this opportunity to express my views on the 
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (Amendment) 
Bill, 2000. Though the original Act was enacted in the year 1981, the 
(Amendment) Bill has been brought now by the hon. Finance Minister. 
The amendment sought in this B ill is that the capital has been 
increased from Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 5,000 crores. I welcome the Bill 
for the following reasons. We could see in the Bill that in respect of 26 
sections, amendments have been brought by way of additions, 
deletions, insertions and substitutions. Not only has the capital been 
increased from Rs. 500 crores to Rs. 5000 crores, further, the Board 
of Management has been constituted in accordance with the 
provisions contemplated in t he Bill. That apart, the reason for my 
welcoming the Bill is that, now am ong the Board of Directors, four 
directors from the State Government officials could participate. Such 
a provision has been cont emplated In the Bill. As far as the D.M.K. 
party is concerned and the State is concerned, we are pleading for 
the State's autonomy, and now, in this Bill, a provis ion has been 
made allowing the participation of four directors. In the Objects and 
Reasons of the Bill, we could see the reason for bringing forward this 
Bill. While Implementing the provisi ons of the Nati onal Bank for 
Agriculture and Rural Development Act, 1981, several bottlenecks 
and shortcomings have come to light. Hence, with a view to removing 
them and providing functional autonomy and operational flexibility to 
the banks as well as expanding its role and augmenting its resources 
to make it a strong, self-reliant and more vibrant institution so as to 
effectively save the agriculture and rural sector In

consonance with the present policy of liberalisation and reforms, 
several amendments have been brought in this legislation. As far as 
NABARD is concerned, people get the financial help through the 
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, which is an 
Apex Development Bank in the field of agriculture and rural 
development. Its main function is to provide refiance to various 
functioning institutions, such as State Cooperative Banks, Regional 
Rural Banks and Commercial Banks for promotion of agriculture, 
small-scale industries, cottage and village industries and allied 
activities in rural areas with a view to promoting integrated rural 
development and securing prospersity for rural areas. So, the sole 
and the main objective of NABARD is to finance the banks which 
have been mentioned by me, and through those banks, the people 
are deriving the help. In the Preamble, it is stated: 
"An Act to establish a development bank to be known 
as the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural 
Development for providing and regulating credit and 
other facilities fo r the promot ion and development of 
agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village 
industries, handicrafts and other rural crafts and other 
allied economic activities in rural areas with a view to 
promoting integrated  rural development and securing 
prosperity of rural areas and for matters connected 
therewith or incidental thereto." 
Madam Deputy Chairperson, as far as India is concerned, it is 
agriculture   oriented   country,   and   if   we   take   into   
consideration   the agriculturists and also the people who are involved 
in village industri es,handicrafts and other rural cra fts and other allied 
economic activities in rural areas, definitely,  out of 100 crores of 
people, more than 80 crores are involved in all these professions, 
namely, agriculture and other professions. My respectful appeal to the 
Minister Is this.   As far as India is concerned, by straining every 
nerve, the village agriculturists and their womenfolk have brought the 
production of foodgrains,  namely,  wheat,  paddy and other grains, 
and have converted India into a surplus State.   My hon. friend and a 
senior Member, Mr. Gautam, when he addressed the issue, brought 
to the attention of the hon. Minist er that amongst the Directors, who 
are going to take part in the Board of Management, the agriculturists 
are not included. In the proviso it is stated: 
"Provided that until the assumption of charge by the 
elected directors under this clause, the Central 
Government may at any time nominate such number

directors not exceeding four from amongst persons 
having special knowledge of, and professional 
experience In, agricultural science, technology, 
economics, banking, cooperatives, law, rural finance, 
investment, accountancy, marketing or any other 
matter, the special knowledge of, and professional 
experience in, which would, in the opinion of the 
Central Government, be useful to the National Bank 
for carryng out its functions." 
I appeal to the Minister that there should be a mandatory 
provision. The Central Government shall nominate not less than four 
directors, and that too, after removing all these provisions, there 
should be tillers of the soil only. From amongst the agriculturists, four 
directors shouW be nominated on the Board of Management. Not 
only that; as far as India is concerned, all the womenfolk are working 
like anything. In fact, they work more than men in villages to augment 
the production of foodgrains. On a perusal of this Amendment Bill, I 
was not able to see any provision In this Bill for the nomination of 
women-directors. We see that everywhere a voice is being raised that 
33 per cent seats should be reserved in the Assemblies and in the 
Parliament. When the womenfolk are involved in agricultural 
operations, there should also be  a provision In  this Bill for 
participation by women-directors. Therefore, I appeal to the hon. 
Minister that suitable provisions should be made in this Act to ensure 
the participation of women directors so that they can raise their voice, 
as and when the necessity arises, 
Apart from that, there is one more appeal, Madam. As far as-
the authorised capital is concerned, this amount of Rs.5,000 crores is 
very meagre. If you take the po pulation of this country into 
consideration-now, it is 100 crores--if you take this 100 crores of 
people as a bank, every year, one-and-a-half crores of people are 
deposited in this population bank. Likewise, the authorised capital of 
this Bank should also be increased so that all these refinancing 
institutions, the State Co-operative Societies and other banks, would 
be able to help the agriculturists and also the people engaged in 
small industries, handicrafts, and others which are mentioned here in 
this Bill. I appeal to the hon. Minister that these things should also be 
taken into consideration. With these words, I thank you, Madam, for 
giving me this opportunity. I suppor t and welcome this Bill, on behalf 
of our party which is a partner in the NDA Government.

SHRI R. MARGABANDU .(Tamil Nadu): Madam, I am not 
prepared to suppor t this Bill, unless an a ssurance is given by the 
Government that there will be a proper management of the banking 
system. Otherwise, there is no use of passing this Bill and increasing

banking sector. The purpose of this Bill is for the promotion and 
development of agriculture, small-scale and cottage and village 
industries, for rural development, securing prosperity for the rural

loan; first is the agriculturist, the other is the big landlord; and the third

to them. If at all any loan is given, they will have to pay 10 per cent or

prepared to pay that. After availing of the loan, they do not repay it.

earned crores of rupees and not repaid it? Who are the persons?

you say that it is for the benefit of the agriculturists? How do you say

areas? The sorry state of affairs is continuing. I quote one instance.

the poor people who are availing of a loan of Rs. 1,000 or Rs. 2,000

not repaying - the loan amount on account of failure
